1. D-(-)-glucose and L-(+)-fructose both have the same molecular formula, C6H12O6, so the difference is not in the molecular formula.

2. D-(-)-glucose has an aldehyde group (making it an aldose), while L-(+)-fructose has a ketone group (making it a ketose). Thus, they differ in the number of aldehyde groups.

3. Both D-(-)-glucose and L-(+)-fructose have six carbon atoms, so the number of carbons is the same.

4. Both sugars have the same number of hydroxyl (-OH) groups, as they share the molecular formula C6H12O6.

5. D-(-)-glucose and L-(+)-fructose are enantiomers, which means they bend light in opposite directions.

6. D-(-)-glucose has 4 chiral centers, while L-(+)-fructose also has 4 chiral centers, so the number of chiral centers is the same.

Based on this analysis, the differences are that they bend light in opposite directions and have different numbers of aldehyde groups.
